articles.title: Ukraine deals major blow to Putin’s Crimea lifeline, European intel assessment claims
articles.summary:
Ukraine's repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge, one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prized infrastructure projects, have dealt a potentially significant blow to Moscow's military supply routes into occupied Crimea, raising questions about Russia's ability to sustain operations as both sides prepare for a difficult winter.

A European intelligence assessment dated Nov. 18 and obtained by Fox News Digital describes Ukraine's latest assault as likely its most successful attack on the heavily defended crossing, following a coordinated campaign targeting Russian air defenses, radar and electronic warfare systems.

Ret. Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told Fox News Digital the consequences could extend far beyond the destruction of a symbolic Russian landmark. "The Russians are extremely limited in how they get supplies to Crimea and cutting the Kerch bridge will severely, severely damage their ability to resupply Crimea," Breedlove said.

UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'

On Nov. 17, Ukrainian missiles and drones struck the 12-mile bridge linking Russia's Krasnodar region to Crimea, collapsing a major section of the roadway into the Kerch Strait and damaging the adjacent railway.

The crossing, inaugurated by Putin in 2018, has served as both a critical transportation link and a symbol of Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014.

According to the European intelligence assessment, the attack followed a multiweek Ukrainian operation against Russian defensive systems, intended to weaken the bridge's protection before the main strike.

Ukraine subsequently struck the railway again on Nov.19, temporarily halting train traffic and bringing the number of attacks to three in four days.

The damage has disrupted one of Russia's most direct supply connections to Crimea, which Moscow uses to support military operations in southern Ukraine.

PUTIN LAUNCHES UKRAINE BARRAGE HOURS AFTER TRUMP MEETING AMID ALLEGED RUSSIAN MISSILE BREACH OF NATO AIRSPACE

Russia has developed an alternative land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, but the European intelligence assessment warns that shifting additional military supplies onto those roads could create significant vulnerabilities.

The assessment identifies slower transportation routes, exposure to Ukrainian drone attacks and pressure on other logistical infrastructure as potential consequences.

Breedlove said Ukraine's campaign should be viewed as an attempt to weaken Russia's hold on the peninsula, rather than simply destroy a bridge. He argued that Russia's options are further constrained by Ukraine's success in challenging Russian naval power in the northern Black Sea.

He pointed out that Ukraine has used maritime and aerial drones to push back Russia's Black Sea Fleet despite lacking large conventional warships.

The European assessment also warns that repairing the bridge could take months. Although limited road traffic might resume within weeks, replacing the collapsed section could take considerably longer, particularly if Ukrainian attacks continue.

Damage above the Kerch–Yenikale Canal could also disrupt shipping between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS

Despite Ukraine's success in striking the bridge, a European intelligence source familiar with Russian strategic assessments offered a pessimistic view of the broader conflict.

"It has more symbolic meaning, but also logistics is paralyzed right now," the source told Fox News Digital, describing the immediate impact of the attacks.

However, the source warned that Moscow is preparing to intensify its winter offensive while using negotiations with Washington to increase political pressure on Kyiv.

"The general trend is not good for Ukraine," the source said.

According to the source, Russia believes it can sustain military pressure long enough to force Ukraine into territorial concessions, particularly in the east.

"They are very convinced that by spring Ukrainians will give up," the source said, describing Moscow's expectations.

Breedlove strongly disputed the assessment that Russia was gaining the upper hand militarily.

"Militarily, the tide is turning against Russia," Breedlove told Fox News Digital, arguing that Russian forces have suffered staggering casualties while making limited battlefield gains.

He said Russian losses in recent months had been extraordinarily high and argued that Moscow's military was failing to achieve significant territorial advances.

Breedlove did, however, acknowledge a distinction between military momentum and the political pressure facing Ukraine.

He suggested that changes in Washington's approach to negotiations could strengthen Putin's position even if Russian forces were struggling on the battlefield.

The competing assessments highlight a central question facing Ukraine: whether its military successes can translate into greater diplomatic leverage before Russia's winter offensive intensifies.

UKRAINE STRIKES 'ONE OF THE LARGEST OIL REFINERIES' IN SOUTHERN RUSSIA AHEAD OF PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING IN CHINA

Putin has threatened retaliation over the bridge attacks, and on Friday Russia launched a massive missile and drone assault against Ukrainian cities, killing at least eight people, according to Ukrainian authorities.

The strikes came hours after Putin appeared alongside President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit in China, as Washington continued efforts to advance peace negotiations.

The European intelligence assessment warns that further Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Bridge during repairs are highly likely, potentially prolonging disruptions to Russian supplies.

For Moscow, restoring the crossing is now both a logistical challenge and a political priority. For Kyiv, keeping it vulnerable offers a way to increase the cost of Russia's occupation while demonstrating that even Putin's most heavily defended infrastructure remains within reach.

articles.title: New drug combo shrinks tumors in most patients facing aggressive cancer type
articles.summary:
Pairing an experimental pill with standard chemotherapy shrank tumors or halted growth in most patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, according to early clinical trial results presented Friday at a major international cancer conference.

The findings, shared at the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium in Barcelona, come from a phase ½ trial testing a daily oral medication called daraxonrasib, along with two standard intravenous chemotherapy drugs, gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel.

The trial focused on 61 patients whose pancreatic cancer had already spread to other organs and who had not yet received treatment for their advanced disease.

PANCREATIC CANCER PATIENT BEN SASSE SEES 'MASSIVE' TUMOR REDUCTION WITH EXPERIMENTAL NEW DRUG

Pancreatic cancer is notoriously difficult to treat because more than half of patients are diagnosed after the disease has already spread, research shows.

In major clinical trials for metastatic pancreatic cancer, chemotherapy alone shrinks tumors in about 23% to 42% of patients, but the disease typically begins growing again after five to six months, and most patients survive between 8 and 11 months.

According to National Cancer Institute data, only about 3% of patients with distant-stage disease live five years past diagnosis.

In the new study, which tracked patients for a median follow-up of 18 months, tumors shrank in 60.7% of cases, including 8.2% where they disappeared entirely on scans. Overall, the combination stopped tumor growth in 90.2% of participants.

FDA APPROVES ONCE-DAILY PILL FOR DEADLY CANCER AFTER PATIENTS' SURVIVAL RATES NEARLY DOUBLE

Patients went a median of 12.8 months before their cancer worsened, almost double the timeframe typically seen with standard chemotherapy, and 76.6% were still alive at the one-year mark, the study found.

"We are now seeing not only substantial tumor shrinkages, including complete responses, but also durable disease control, with median progression-free survival exceeding one year," study lead Dr. Wungki Park, a gastrointestinal medical oncologist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York, said in a press release.

More than 90% of pancreatic cancers are driven by a faulty gene called RAS, which allows tumors to keep growing. Daraxonrasib is designed to turn off that growth signal, something scientists long thought was impossible to fix with medication.

Dr. Elena Garralda, chair of the symposium and co-director of the clinical research program at the Vall d’Hebron Institute of Oncology in Spain, who was not involved in the research, said the results show that RAS-targeted drugs can be combined with existing treatments at the start of treatment to potentially achieve longer-lasting benefits.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Side effects included rash, diarrhea, fatigue and low blood cell counts linked to chemotherapy, most of which were manageable with standard care.

Only 5% of patients stopped treatment because of side effects tied to daraxonrasib.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Researchers emphasized that the findings carry some limitations.

Because this was an early-phase, single-group study involving 61 people, all participants received the experimental combination. Without a direct comparison group of patients receiving standard chemotherapy alone, doctors cannot yet confirm how much better the new regimen performs or whether it definitively extends overall survival.

The findings also apply strictly to metastatic pancreatic cancer, even though RAS mutations drive several other cancers, including certain lung, colorectal and gynecological cancers. Separate studies would be needed to test whether the combination works in those diseases.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The trial was funded by Revolution Medicines, the California-based developer of daraxonrasib.

To determine whether these early findings translate into a durable survival benefit, researchers have launched a larger, randomized Phase 3 trial, called RASolute-303, which directly compares daraxonrasib — both on its own and combined with chemotherapy — against standard chemotherapy alone.

articles.title: Uber Parking could save you from circling the block
articles.summary:
You finally make it downtown for dinner, but now comes the real challenge. Finding somewhere to park. You circle the block once, then again. Before you know it, you're late and getting frustrated. Sound familiar? Well, Uber thinks it has a solution. The company just launched Uber Parking, a new feature that lets you reserve a parking spot directly through the Uber app before you even leave home. Yes, the same company that built its business around getting you into someone else's car now wants to help when you drive your own. And there's another interesting twist. Uber has plans for those parking garages that involve robotaxis.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

UBER LETS PARENTS WATCH TEEN RIDES LIVE

On Nov. 9, Uber announced the launch of Uber Parking, bringing parking reservations directly into its app. The feature follows Uber's acquisition of SpotHero, a popular parking reservation service. Through that deal, Uber gained access to a network of more than 13,000 parking garages, lots and valet locations across more than 400 cities in the United States and Canada.

So, instead of driving around looking for parking, you can search for an available spot near your destination. You can also see the price upfront, making it easier to decide whether driving makes financial sense. For someone heading into the city for dinner or trying to get to an important appointment, that could save some aggravation. And if you've ever paid a small fortune to park somewhere, you'll probably appreciate being able to compare prices before arriving.

Uber has made the process pretty simple. You can book parking using the same app you already use to request a ride.

Here's how it works:

Once you've booked, your digital parking pass appears inside the Uber app. Depending on the location, you'll either scan a QR code or enter through a system that recognizes your license plate. Uber also says you can extend reservations through the app if you need more time. Cancellation policies vary by parking facility. Some reservations qualify for a full refund if canceled before the scheduled start time. Always check the booking terms before paying.

One thing worth mentioning: Uber generally won't physically park your car for you. Unless you choose a valet location, you'll still be the one behind the wheel.

FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL

Uber Parking launched in 15 U.S. cities on Nov. 9.

Those cities are:

Uber plans to expand the service into additional markets. However, there's an important detail here. Although SpotHero operates across more than 400 cities, Uber Parking has not yet expanded throughout that entire network. Also, the new feature is still rolling out. So, even if you're in one of the launch cities, you may not see the Parking icon immediately. First, make sure you're using the latest version of the Uber app. You can also visit SpotHero's website to search for parking in areas where the Uber feature is unavailable.

Here's a little bonus if you already pay for Uber One. Uber says eligible members can earn 10% back in Uber One credits on qualifying parking reservations once their parking session is complete. You can use those credits toward future eligible Uber rides or Uber Eats orders. For example, if you spend $30 on a qualifying parking reservation, you could earn $3 in Uber One credits.

That may not sound like a fortune. However, if you're regularly parking downtown, those credits could add up. Just keep in mind that the 10% reward only applies to eligible reservations. You also need an active Uber One membership to qualify and redeem the credits. And remember, these are Uber credits rather than cash back to your bank account. Before booking, compare the total parking price with other nearby options. A cheaper garage could still save you more money than the rewards you'd earn.

Uber also sees parking garages as part of its future robotaxi business. Think about it. When a driverless taxi drops someone off, what happens next? If another passenger needs a ride nearby, that's easy enough. But what happens when nobody needs the car? Does it keep driving around until another request comes in? That could mean more empty vehicles on already crowded streets. Uber is reportedly exploring ways to use parking facilities as waiting areas for autonomous vehicles. Instead of driving around without passengers, robotaxis could pull into nearby garages and wait for their next assignment.

Then, when someone requests a ride, the vehicle could head out to pick them up. Uber believes that approach could reduce unnecessary driving and help lower operating costs. There's another potential benefit. Keeping autonomous vehicles in nearby facilities could make it easier to have them ready when demand increases. However, this remains a developing plan. Uber has not announced that every SpotHero garage will accommodate robotaxis, and the company has not provided a timeline for a broad rollout of these facilities. For now, the immediate focus remains helping people find parking for their own cars.

There's something else worth paying attention to here. For years, Uber built its business around giving people an alternative to driving. Now, the company wants you opening its app even when you plan to take your own car. Let's say you're going downtown for dinner. You could check the price of an Uber ride. Then, you could compare that with the cost of driving and parking.

If driving looks cheaper, you can reserve a space through Uber. If taking a ride makes more sense, you can book that instead. Either way, Uber stays part of your plans. And as autonomous vehicles become more common, the company could eventually use that same parking network to support its robotaxi partners. It's an interesting strategy, especially as Uber looks for more ways to keep people using its app.

The biggest benefit is pretty straightforward. You may be able to reserve parking before leaving home and spend less time driving around looking for an available spot. That could be especially useful when you're heading somewhere unfamiliar or trying to make a flight. However, there are a few things I'd recommend checking before you book.

Don't assume Uber offers the lowest rate. Check the final price against other parking options before paying. Also, make sure your reservation covers the time you'll actually need.

Some parking garages have height limits. If you drive a larger SUV or truck, check those restrictions before booking. Also, confirm the exact entrance address, which may differ from the garage's street address.

Some parking reservations can be canceled for free before they begin, but the rules vary by location. Review the specific garage's cancellation terms before booking. Once your reservation starts, Uber says it can no longer be canceled or refunded.

Some garages use QR codes for entry. That's convenient, but criminals have also placed fake QR codes on parking meters to trick drivers into visiting fraudulent payment websites. Use the parking pass provided directly through your Uber app rather than scanning an unfamiliar sticker. We've previously reported on how criminals use fake parking QR codes to steal money.

Even with a reservation, finding your car afterward can still be a headache. Fortunately, Google Maps and Apple Maps have tools that can help you remember where you parked. Our guide to finding your parked car with Maps explains how to set them up.

I think Uber is onto something here. Who hasn't wasted time driving around looking for parking, especially when you're already running late? Being able to reserve a spot before leaving home sounds pretty convenient. Of course, I'd want to make sure I'm getting a good price. But what really caught my attention is Uber's plan to use parking garages for robotaxis. Having driverless cars park between rides makes sense, especially if it means fewer empty vehicles clogging up our streets. Still, I wonder what happens when those garages start filling up with robotaxis. Will there be enough room for the rest of us? That's something I'll be watching as this technology takes off.

Would you trust Uber to handle your parking reservations, or do you worry that parking garages could eventually become crowded with robotaxis, leaving fewer spaces for the rest of us? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Putin launches Ukraine barrage hours after Trump meeting amid alleged Russian missile breach of NATO airspace
articles.summary:
Just hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin stood alongside President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a historic summit in China, Moscow unleashed one of its largest attacks on Ukraine, killing at least eight people, striking three major bridges in Kyiv and sending suspected Russian missiles and a drone into NATO-member Poland.

The massive overnight assault Friday came as the Trump administration announced progress toward expanding peace negotiations with Russia, exposing the stark contrast between the diplomatic optimism emerging from Thursday's meetings and the escalating war on the ground.

A European intelligence source told Fox News Digital that Putin is preparing an intensified winter military campaign and believes that a combination of sustained battlefield pressure and U.S.-led diplomatic negotiations could eventually force Ukraine to surrender additional territory.

TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE

The source described the photograph of Putin standing alongside Trump and Xi as a long-sought diplomatic achievement for the Russian leader, even as Moscow prepares to increase pressure on Kyiv.

According to the source, Russia's calculation is that Ukraine could be compelled to accept territorial concessions by spring, particularly in the country's east.

"They are very convinced that by spring Ukrainians will give up," the source told Fox News Digital, describing what the source assessed to be Moscow's strategy.

The source also warned that Russian military pressure is increasing despite Ukraine's recent successful strikes against critical Russian infrastructure. "It's going to be a very difficult winter for Ukrainians," the source said.

Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told Fox News Digital that the timing of Russia's latest assault should leave little doubt about Putin's intentions, arguing that the Russian leader has repeatedly responded to President Donald Trump's diplomatic overtures with renewed attacks on Ukraine.

"Putin never has been a partner for peace in Ukraine," he said. "And Putin will never be a partner for peace in the future for Ukraine." Breedlove said that Putin's objective is to subjugate Ukraine, install a leadership loyal to Moscow and exploit the country's resources.

RUSSIA PLOTTING 'MASSIVE STRIKE' DURING MIDTERMS, ZELENSKYY WARNS, URGES US TO STOP PUTIN

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, targeting the country's energy, transportation and logistical infrastructure.

The barrage killed six people in Kyiv and two in the western city of Lviv, while more than two dozen others were wounded, according to a Reuters' Nov. 20 report.

Three major bridges spanning the Dnipro River in Kyiv — the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Pivdennyi bridges — were struck, disrupting transportation between the eastern and western sections of the capital.

Russian attacks also damaged railway infrastructure and energy facilities, triggering emergency power outages as temperatures drop ahead of winter.

In Lviv, two people were killed in a strike on the Sknyliv railway station, while additional injuries were reported following attacks on residential buildings and a hospital in other Ukrainian regions.

UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY ON DEFYING US IN ATTACKING RUSSIAN OIL: 'OUR RESPONSE MUST BE PAINFUL'

Zelenskyy accused Moscow of using the attacks to compensate for what he described as military and diplomatic setbacks.

"This was one of the largest attacks," Zelenskyy said in a statement published on Telegram Friday.

Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed carrying out a massive operation, saying it targeted facilities connected to Ukraine's military-industrial complex, including missile and drone production sites and transportation infrastructure.

The competing claims about the targets and the extent of the damage could not be independently verified.

The strikes followed Putin's warning Thursday that Russia would retaliate against Ukraine for repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge, which connects Russia with the occupied Crimean Peninsula.

Ukrainian forces launched three attacks on the strategic crossing in four days, damaging its road section and disrupting rail traffic.

The bridge, inaugurated by Putin in 2018, serves as both a transportation route and a powerful symbol of Moscow's control over Crimea, which Russia annexed in 2014.

UKRAINE STRIKES 'ONE OF THE LARGEST OIL REFINERIES' IN SOUTHERN RUSSIA AHEAD OF PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING IN CHINA

The overnight assault also raised concerns beyond Ukraine's borders after Polish officials reported three separate incursions into the country's airspace.

Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said one of the objects was identified as a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, while another was believed to be a missile and the third likely a jet-powered drone.

Authorities were investigating debris near Nowy Lipowiec, Mołodycz and Rudnik nad Sanem in southeastern Poland.

"There has been a violation of Polish airspace and an incursion by objects from the Russian Federation," Kosiniak-Kamysz said, according to Reuters.

Poland said it would seek additional NATO assistance to secure the alliance's eastern flank.

Breedlove warned that the reported incursions into Polish airspace were part of a broader pattern of Russia testing NATO's resolve. "Mr. Putin will push further and further when there is no cost to him, when NATO doesn't respond, when the United States doesn't respond, in his mind, there is no reason to stop. He will continue," Breedlove told Fox News Digital.

UKRAINE RELEASES VIDEO SHOWING DAMAGE TO PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE FOLLOWING 'UNPRECEDENTED OPERATION' IN CRIMEA

The attacks came less than a day after the Trump administration announced what it described as progress toward a broader diplomatic framework involving Russia, Ukraine and European governments.

During talks in Berlin Thursday, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Moscow had agreed to engage in an expanded negotiating format that would include European representatives.

"Russia has agreed to engage in the multilateral format with the Europeans," Kushner said, according to Fox News Digital's Nov. 19 report.

Zelenskyy urged Washington to organize the next round of discussions quickly, insisting that European governments must play a full role in negotiations affecting the continent's security.

But Moscow's position remained less clear Friday, with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov saying an invitation for European officials to visit Moscow did not mean they had been accepted into the existing U.S.-brokered negotiating format, according to The Associated Press.

The European intelligence source suggested Russia believes the diplomatic process itself could strengthen its negotiating position by allowing Moscow to broaden discussions beyond Ukrainian territory to the future security arrangements of Europe.

According to the source, Moscow is seeking to gain time, maintain military pressure and increasingly focus negotiations on wider European security questions.

The source also described Russian efforts to maintain troop numbers without announcing another large-scale nationwide mobilization.

"They have been able to avoid open mobilization, but they have hidden mobilization," the source said.

According to the source, Russian recruitment efforts include targeting people facing financial difficulties, debt or other social vulnerabilities, alongside continued recruitment from prisons.

RUSSIA'S PUTIN VOWS A RESPONSE 'FAR MORE PAINFUL' AFTER UKRAINE ATTACKS PRIZED BRIDGE IN CRIMEA

The source argued that Moscow is prioritizing manpower over the quality and training of new recruits.

"More quantity, less quality," the source said, warning that inadequately prepared recruits face a greater risk of being killed on the battlefield.

Those recruitment claims have not been independently verified by Fox News Digital.

The source's broader assessment was that Russia believes it can sustain military operations long enough to increase pressure on Ukraine's leadership to accept territorial concessions.

For Kyiv, the latest barrage demonstrated the immediate challenge facing U.S.-led peace efforts: negotiations are advancing while Moscow continues large-scale military operations and Ukraine strikes strategic targets deep inside Russian-held territory.

The events also highlighted the growing risks for NATO as the consequences of Russia's war extend beyond Ukraine's borders.

Reuters and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Senate foreign relations chairman warns of 'horrific trend' as Christians killed in Ethiopia
articles.summary:
The Republican chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has warned of an ongoing ‘horrific trend’ of Christians being killed in Africa.

Earlier this month, at least 34 people, the majority said to be Ethiopian Orthodox Christians, were killed in a village in the Arsi Zone, about 250 miles southeast of Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa.

"The attacks on Christians in Ethiopia are a horrific trend," Sen. Jim Risch, R-Idaho, told Fox News Digital in a statement, adding, "The instability and violence in Ethiopia has grave consequences for Ethiopian civilians, the region and American interests."

NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Open Doors UK & Ireland told Fox News Digital there has been a string of killings in the area, with some 60 Orthodox Christians killed just two weeks before this attack in November. Open Doors is an international organization supporting persecuted Christians.

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital they are aware of "reports of killing in Arsi Zone," adding: "Reports of civilian killings in Ethiopia demand action. We call for independent investigations and accountability."

The Addis Standard online news outlet reported gunmen approached St. Mary’s Church in Endeto, Robe District, and at the main entrance shouted "Surrender" before opening fire. Worshipers here are from the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Local security guards, who are said to have fired back to protect community members, are believed to be among the dead.

One resident told the Addis Standard, "If you asked me right now, I have no hope of staying here because I would choose to flee for long-term survival."

The identity of the attackers has not yet been confirmed. An attack last month has been attributed locally to the Oromo Liberation Army, designated in Ethiopia as a terrorist organization.

The State Department, quoting the Ethiopian government’s 2007 census, the most recent available, stated the country’s population is 63% Christian. One local source reports though that three of those who died in this latest attack were Muslim.

SUPER BOWL CHAMP BEN WATSON SPEAKS OUT ON CHRISTIAN NIGERIAN PERSECUTION, DOUBLE-STANDARDS AND TRUMP'S IMPACT

Ethiopia is ranked 36 on Open Doors’ World Watch List of countries where Christians are most persecuted. The organization stated "Open Doors condemns the violence against Orthodox Christians and calls on the Government of Ethiopia to take proactive measures to protect vulnerable civilians from attacks by armed groups operating in the area. Reports from the field point to horrific brutality against Orthodox Christians in parts of the Arsi zone of Oromia."

The statement continued, "We urge the federal government to protect vulnerable communities, including Orthodox Christians, particularly in areas where armed groups are active. We also call on the government to hold perpetrators accountable and help all those affected rebuild their lives."

ANOTHER CHRISTIAN COMMUNITY AT RISK IN AFRICA AS EXTREMISTS AND WAR TAKE THEIR TOLL

Open Doors states the recent attacks in the area started in 2025, when 25 people were killed. 

The attacks have ramped up this year:

In February, attackers stormed a church and a market in East Arsi, killing more than 20 Orthodox Christians and one Muslim guard.

In March, 21 people were reportedly killed in East Arsi Zone.

In May, the 101-year-old Teleta Holy Gabriel Church was destroyed and 50 killed in multiple attacks.

In October, 14 people were killed in Gora Singo and in the Arsi Zone, 46 were killed in multiple attacks. This led to the U.S. Ambassador to Ethiopia Ervin J. Masinga posting, "Such horrific attacks against any group must stop."

In November, at least 34 were killed in Endeto.

Senate Foreign Affairs Chairman Risch added, "It is imperative that Ethiopia find a way to manage its domestic affairs in a way that addresses longstanding grievances and promotes sustained peace."

With fighting continuing in several parts of the country, especially in the border area around Eritrea, the State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "Fighting in several regions of Ethiopia is a concern. We urge all parties to protect civilians and resolve disputes through dialogue."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Ethiopian government, but received no response.

articles.title: Hackers use Microsoft Outlook security flaw to steal your login data
articles.summary:
You probably know better than to enter your password on a suspicious website. But what if hackers could steal information tied to your Windows login without ever asking for your password? That's the concern behind a Microsoft Outlook security flaw that hackers are already exploiting. Attackers can trick someone into opening a malicious Outlook file that quietly exposes Windows authentication information. That information could help a criminal impersonate you and potentially gain access to systems you use.

Microsoft released a fix on Nov. 10. However, the company confirms hackers were exploiting the vulnerability before the update became available. If you use Outlook for work, this is one security update you should check right away.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FAKE AI EVENT INVITES TARGET MICROSOFT AND GOOGLE LOGINS

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, involves how Outlook handles specially crafted message files. An attacker can create a malicious Outlook message file, such as one using the .msg format. The hacker then needs to convince someone to open that file in an affected version of Outlook. Once opened, the malicious file can cause Outlook to connect to a server controlled by the attacker. That connection happens without the usual warning about accessing external content. During the connection, Windows can reveal NTLMv2 authentication information. This data helps Windows verify your identity when connecting to certain network services.

The information differs from your actual password. However, hackers may be able to use it in a follow-up attack to impersonate you. For someone using Outlook at work, that could potentially expose company resources their account can access. The outcome depends on the network's security protections and whether the attacker can successfully misuse the authentication information. Here's what makes this especially concerning. The attack doesn't require you to type your password into a fake login page. Opening the malicious file can be enough if your computer can connect to the attacker's network location. Microsoft says simply viewing the message through Outlook's Preview Pane does not trigger this particular vulnerability. Someone must open the malicious file for the attack to work.

Microsoft included the Outlook fix in its November Patch Tuesday security updates. The company's core release addressed 1,093 vulnerabilities, including 63 rated critical. Interestingly, Microsoft classified this particular Outlook vulnerability as moderate, giving it a CVSS severity score of 6.5 out of 10. However, that rating tells only part of the story. Microsoft confirms attackers have already exploited the flaw. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov. 10. In other words, hackers are already taking advantage of this security weakness. Microsoft has not publicly identified who carried out the attacks or disclosed how many people were affected. The company also hasn't provided detailed information about the incidents. With hackers already exploiting the flaw, it's important to install the security update as soon as possible.

FAKE CHATGPT BILLING EMAILS CAN STEAL YOUR LOGIN

According to Microsoft's security advisory, the affected products include:

The vulnerability concerns affected desktop Office installations on Windows computers. Microsoft's advisory does not list Outlook.com in a web browser or the Outlook mobile apps as affected products. If your employer manages your Microsoft 365 software, your IT department may handle these updates. However, it's worth confirming that the security fix has been installed. For people who manage their own computers, here's how to check.

The most important thing you can do is update Microsoft Office. However, a few additional precautions can help reduce your exposure to suspicious files and account attacks.

Microsoft has released security updates addressing the vulnerability. You can manually check for updates in supported Windows versions of Office.

If you don't see Update Now, you may need to select Enable Updates first. If the entire Update Options menu is missing, your employer may manage updates centrally. Contact your IT department rather than assuming the software has already been patched. You can also review Microsoft's official Office update instructions.

After installing the update, you can check which version of Office is running on your computer.

For affected volume-licensed installations, Microsoft's November 10 security release includes these updated builds:

These build numbers apply to the specified LTSC editions. They shouldn't be used to check other Office versions. If you're using Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, the correct build depends on your organization's update channel. You can check Microsoft's Office security release notes or contact your IT department to confirm the fix.

Although this vulnerability requires an Office fix, keeping Windows updated remains important.

On Windows 11:

Next, check whether Windows can receive updates for other Microsoft products.

This can help Windows deliver updates for supported Microsoft products. However, some Office installations receive updates through separate services or employer-managed systems. Remember that checking Windows Update alone may not confirm you've installed the specific Outlook fix. Check Office separately. It's also smart to back up important files before installing major operating system updates.

A message file from an unfamiliar sender deserves extra caution, especially if you weren't expecting it. Watch for attachments ending in .msg, a common file format for saved Outlook messages. The format itself is legitimate. However, attackers can abuse it to deliver this exploit. If an email claims you need to open an attached message to review an invoice or urgent workplace request, verify it through another trusted channel. Even attachments appearing to come from coworkers deserve a second look when the request seems unusual.

If something looks suspicious, avoid opening the attachment. Instead, report the message using Outlook's built-in reporting tools when available.

In supported versions of Outlook:

The exact menu location depends on your Outlook version and your employer's settings. If you're using a work account and don't see a reporting option, contact your IT department. Avoid forwarding the suspicious attachment to other coworkers.

Strong antivirus software can help identify suspicious attachments and malicious activity before they cause further damage. Look for protection that includes real-time scanning and behavior-based detection. These features may help catch threats that traditional virus signatures miss. However, antivirus software cannot replace Microsoft's security patch. Installing the Outlook update remains essential for closing this particular vulnerability. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

Multifactor authentication (MFA) adds another layer of account protection by requiring additional verification when you sign in. Enable it on your Microsoft account and other important services whenever available. Keep in mind that MFA may not stop attacks involving stolen Windows authentication information. That's another reason updating Outlook takes priority.

If you recently opened an unexpected Outlook message attachment, don't assume everything is fine because nothing unusual appeared on your screen. Here's what to do next.

One important reminder: Changing your password alone may not address every potential exposure from this vulnerability. If you opened the attachment on a work computer, let your IT team determine whether additional security measures are necessary.

Microsoft's November security release covers far more than Outlook. It also fixes weaknesses that could allow attackers to gain additional privileges or remotely execute malicious code. For those of you using a Windows PC every day, the sheer number of vulnerabilities may sound overwhelming. However, not every flaw carries the same immediate risk. In this case, the Outlook weakness deserves your attention because Microsoft has confirmed active exploitation.

The larger concern is how easily a malicious file can take advantage of trusted software. Outlook is part of everyday communication for countless businesses, and opening saved email messages may seem harmless. This vulnerability shows why keeping Office updated deserves the same attention as updating Windows.

What concerns me about this Outlook flaw is how little someone has to do to put their information at risk. You could receive what looks like a routine work attachment, open it and unknowingly expose information that helps a hacker impersonate you. There's no obvious warning telling you something went wrong. And by the time you realize it, the damage may already be done. I also find it troubling that Microsoft rated this vulnerability moderate even though attackers were already exploiting it. Most people aren't going to spend their day reviewing security ratings, and they shouldn't have to. They need software that protects them and updates that are easy to install. My advice is simple. If you use Outlook on a Windows computer, check for Office updates today. Don't assume your computer has already taken care of it.

Should Microsoft be doing more to prevent a single malicious Outlook file from exposing your login information, or do you think keeping your software updated is enough protection? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: Mysterious illness tied to breast implants shares symptoms with MS, but key questions remain
articles.summary:
Weeks after Christina Applegate revealed she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS), the actress has shared a suspicion that her breast implants could be to blame for her symptoms.

On a Nov. 10 episode of the podcast "MeSsy," which she co-hosts with actress and MS advocate Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Applegate — who underwent a double mastectomy in 2008 after a breast cancer diagnosis — said she believes she is overdue to have her implants replaced.

Applegate also said she recently saw a study suggesting that implant-related symptoms could resemble MS.

CHRISTINA APPLEGATE'S MS MISDIAGNOSIS AFTER 5 YEARS OF TREATMENT EXPOSES ALARMING MEDICAL REALITY

"And I swear, over the last five years or whatever, I thought, ‘What if they’re leaking, and they’re like poisoning me?’" she said.

Applegate said she plans to discuss the possibility with her doctors. She did not say that her implants had been confirmed as the cause.

Some of her symptoms have included joint pain, difficulty lifting her right arm and pain that can make it hard to get out of bed, she shared during the episode.

"I don’t know what’s going on in my joints, but I can’t move my right shoulder at all now," she said. "I can’t lift my arm."

NYC MARATHON RUNNER, 24, DIES JUST 2 MILES FROM FINISH LINE AFTER SENDING DAD CHILLING TEXTS

Other possible conditions that could contribute to these symptoms include rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and Lyme disease, Applegate said.

"We’re going into square one, just doing some testing and going one by one [through] the sister diseases to MS," she added. "It’s overwhelming because there are so many different things that could be going on and this pain stuff."

Diana Zuckerman, Ph.D., president of the National Center for Health Research and a breast implant safety advocate in Washington, D.C., said that breast implant illness hasn’t always gotten a lot of attention, but is being taken more seriously in recent years.

"It’s a range of symptoms, and not everybody has the same symptoms," she told Fox News Digital. "And some of them are pretty common, such as joint pain or chronic fatigue. Some women talk about feeling like they've had the flu for [months]."

Brain fog, memory issues, anxiety, insomnia, muscle pain and weakness are additional symptoms that could potentially overlap with various viruses or conditions.

Women with breast implant illness tend to have many symptoms all at once, Zuckerman said. "They're often very young women who are in their 20s, and suddenly they feel like they're in their 50s — that's how they describe it."

Research has shown that in some cases, if the implants are taken out, women recover "almost miraculously and immediately and dramatically," Zuckerman said.

Jonathan Kaplan, M.D., a board-certified plastic surgeon at Pacific Heights Plastic Surgery in San Francisco, agrees that breast implant illness symptoms are real.

"While patients may have abnormal blood tests to support their concerns about having some type of illness, these lab tests would not predict ahead of time if the patient is more or less likely to have issues if they choose to get implants," he told Fox News Digital.

For those experiencing symptoms such as fatigue, joint or muscle pain, and cognitive concerns, Kaplan recommends starting by looking for other treatable causes, which might include MS or effects of medications.

"The cause could be due to breast implants, but the only way to confirm that is to remove the implants and see if the patient improves," he said. "If they do not, then they may have unnecessarily undergone a surgical procedure that did not benefit them."

MYSTERIOUS DISEASE SENDING YOUNG, HEALTHY TEXAS WORKERS INTO KIDNEY FAILURE

For women who are considering explant surgery, Kaplan asks them how they would feel if they removed the implants and the symptoms persist.

"If they've run out of other options or causes of their illness, they may feel like it is worth the risk of having a procedure even if it doesn't help their illness," he said. "There's no evidence at this time that MS would be affected by the presence or absence of implants."

Kaplan shared that he once had a patient who received breast implants and then several years later experienced fatigue and had abnormal bloodwork suggestive of kidney failure.

"Once she removed her implants, she felt better and labs returned to normal," he said. "But we couldn't have gotten any lab ahead of time that would have predicted her risk of breast implant-associated illness."

Patricia McGuire, M.D., a St. Louis-based plastic surgeon and chair of the Breast Implant Emergency Task Force, noted that over 100 symptoms have been reported by patients in association with breast implant illness.

"They have no abnormal labs or physical findings, and there is no diagnostic criteria," she told Fox News Digital. "It is a diagnosis of exclusion and is not a currently recognized illness."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Symptoms can occur with all types of implants, she noted – silicone gel, saline, smooth and textured implants, by all manufacturers.

"We do not know the cause," McGuire said. "The suggestions have been heavy metals from the implants entering the body, bacterial biofilms, fungal infections, allergic reactions, immune response to a foreign body and neuropsychiatric conditions."

"We also know that some patients may get better with implant removal."

In a prospective, blinded study that McGuire co-led with Dr. Caroline Glicksman, researchers found no biological differences — such as heavy metals, bacteria or inflammatory blood markers — between women reporting breast implant illness and asymptomatic control groups.

Instead, the research revealed that while patients experienced genuine symptom relief after implant removal, the condition was strongly linked to elevated anxiety, somatic symptom patterns and a heavy reliance on social media for medical information, she said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"To be honest, we were disappointed that we did not find an easily reversible cause, or that we did not find a blood value that could be used to make a diagnosis or point to the cause of symptoms in these patients," McGuire added.

"We have a couple of pilot studies in the works, hoping we can find something definitive."

In 2021, the FDA issued strict new labeling rules requiring a boxed warning and a mandatory patient decision checklist for all breast implants. 

The warning explicitly lists systemic symptoms, such as fatigue, memory loss, rash, "brain fog" and joint pain, and notes that symptoms may resolve after removal.

Breast implants are not considered lifetime devices. The FDA recommends routine MRI or ultrasound screenings starting five to six years after surgery (and every two to three years after) to check for "silent" ruptures. 

However, implants do not have a strict 10-year expiration date if they are intact and the patient is asymptomatic.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Anyone with breast implants who experiences symptoms should undergo a full medical work-up to rule out reversible causes before having surgery, McGuire advised.

"For a patient considering implant removal, they should see a board-certified plastic surgeon who has experience in breast surgery," she added.

Fox News Digital reached out to implant manufacturers requesting comment.

articles.title: Former Secret Service investigator sounds alarm over AI scams as Americans grow increasingly anxious
articles.summary:
A former Secret Service cyberfraud investigator warned that Americans are increasingly on edge following a wave of major technology disruptions, while artificial intelligence is making scams targeting families and consumers more sophisticated.

Jason Brown, a former U.S. Secret Service cyberfraud investigator and iCounter's director of customer advisory and counter fraud lead, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Americans have reason to be increasingly cautious about technology.

"Everybody's on edge," Brown said.

"There's been a lot of stuff that has happened in the past week in particular that people are concerned about," he continued, citing recent technology outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and several financial institutions.

TIMELINE: AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

Brown acknowledged that some incidents involved infrastructure problems while others remained under investigation.

With the holiday season approaching, Brown warned that AI has made it easier for criminals to create convincing fraudulent messages, eliminating many of the warning signs consumers previously relied on.

"AI has just made the criminal a lot more efficient and a little bit more effective," Brown said.

Spelling mistakes, poor grammar and awkward phrasing — once common indicators of fraudulent messages — are becoming less reliable as criminals use AI to generate more convincing communications, he explained.

AI VOICE SCAM TRAPS MOM IN 5-HOUR KIDNAPPING NIGHTMARE

AI also allows criminals to impersonate familiar voices, potentially tricking victims into believing they are speaking with a family member in distress.

Brown described a scenario in which a scammer uses a short voice recording to impersonate someone's relative and demand thousands of dollars in gift cards.

"AI just makes them a lot more efficient and a lot less prone to errors," he said, warning that Americans must become more skeptical of suspicious messages.

"Unfortunately, we're at a point where everybody needs to have that level of distrust," he said.

As holiday shopping ramps up, Brown said scammers are likely to impersonate major delivery companies, including UPS, FedEx and the U.S. Postal Service.

FAKE E-ZPASS EMAIL THREATENS $100 FINE OVER UNPAID TOLL

He warned that fraudulent messages may claim packages cannot be delivered until additional postage is paid, with scammers demanding payment through cryptocurrency or gift cards.

"If it comes from crypto, especially if it comes from gift cards, that's a red flag for sure," Brown said.

Beyond the emotional toll, Brown warned that increasingly sophisticated scams can result in significant financial losses. He cited FBI reporting that he said identified more than 22,000 AI-related fraud cases in 2025, with losses exceeding $890 million.

Brown noted that businesses are also vulnerable to schemes in which criminals impersonate trusted vendors and redirect legitimate payments into fraudulent accounts.

AGING MEANS LEARNING HOW TO PREVENT COSTLY SCAMS TARGETING OLDER AMERICANS

The holiday season can create additional vulnerabilities as executives travel, employees take time off and temporary workers join company operations, he said.

Brown urged Americans to independently verify suspicious messages and take additional precautions when communicating with family members, including establishing a "safe word" to help confirm someone's identity during an unexpected call.

"Another thing that we always talk about with family members, set up a safe word ahead of time. Have that conversation now," he said, adding that even if a caller provides the correct word, people should still end the call and contact the person independently using a trusted number.

"The biggest safety valve for anybody in a scam when it comes over the internet via your cell phone, over the computer is stop, think and then independently verify," he added.

articles.title: Zelenskyy presses US for expanded Russia talks as Kushner announces breakthrough
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting.

He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe.

"We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said.

The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks.

KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

"From the very beginning, Ukraine has advocated for this approach — maximum coordination among us on everything concerning European and Ukrainian security and our future," Zelenskyy said.

"We need to work quickly, and this is the only approach Ukraine is taking. The more actively the discussions move forward, the greater the chances of achieving real progress."

According to Kushner, Russia agreed to the expanded negotiating format, including a recent breakthrough on prisoner exchanges.

"Russia has agreed to engage in the multilateral format with the Europeans. Part of that was us explaining to the Russians that we do believe that Russia having Europe at the table will be essential to ending this war in a just and long-term, durable way," Kushner said.

"There's going to be thousands of prisoners of war who will be going home to their families in the next weeks, which will be, obviously, a great gesture and a great relief for people."

FRENCH TROOPS SECRETLY DEPLOYED INSIDE UKRAINE AS EX-NATO CHIEF PRAISES MACRON'S 'GUTS'

He added that President Donald Trump will not impose a unilateral deal but will work with allies to finalize postwar security guarantees.

"President Trump wants to make a deal with Europe by his side. He's not looking to impose anything unilaterally," Kushner said.

"Our goal is really to end this war and to really help build a durable peace. We are very committed. President Trump will do whatever it takes to do that."

articles.title: Popular alcoholic drinks linked to sudden kidney damage in 14-year study
articles.summary:
People who regularly drink beer or hard liquor face a significantly higher risk of sudden kidney damage than light drinkers, while wine drinkers do not show the same increased risk, according to a large British study.

Researchers at Anglia Ruskin University analyzed health and lifestyle data from 250,791 adult drinkers in the UK Biobank database, tracking them for an average of 14 years.

Over that time, 10,335 participants developed acute kidney injury, a serious condition in which the kidneys suddenly stop filtering waste from the blood properly.

IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

The study, published in the journal Scientific Reports, challenges a longstanding medical assumption that alcohol harms the kidneys mainly as a secondary consequence of liver disease.

The elevated risk among beer and liquor drinkers continued even after researchers considered liver disease and a wide range of other health and lifestyle factors.

"Acute kidney injury is a serious condition that can lead to chronic kidney disease, kidney failure and an increased risk of dying early," lead author Rudolph Schutte, an associate professor of cardiovascular epidemiology at Anglia Ruskin University, said in a university news release.

"While alcohol has traditionally been linked with kidney injury through its impact on the liver, our research suggests that spirits and beer may contribute directly to kidney damage through inflammatory pathways."

HEAVY DRINKING SURGES AMONG AMERICANS IN ONE AGE GROUP AS OTHER GENERATIONS CUT BACK

To compare drinking habits, the researchers divided participants into three groups based on their average weekly consumption of each type of alcohol. 

In the U.K., one unit of alcohol equals 8 grams of pure alcohol — a little more than half of a standard U.S. shot of liquor or about half a pint of lower-strength beer.

Among liquor drinkers, those in the lowest consumption group drank an average of 1.22 units per week. Compared with that group, people who averaged 2.69 units per week were 8.1% more likely to develop acute kidney injury. 

Those in the highest tier, averaging 8.73 units per week, had a 25.5% higher risk.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Beer drinkers showed a similar, though smaller, pattern. Compared with light beer drinkers averaging 2.67 units per week, people who drank an average of 6.81 units had a 5.7% higher risk of acute kidney injury. 

Those in the highest group, averaging 23.6 units per week, faced a 14.8% higher risk

Researchers found no significant link between red or white wine consumption and a higher risk of acute kidney injury overall. 

The authors noted that higher levels of internal inflammation appeared to drive the increased risk seen with other drinks.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"The results provide important population-level evidence supporting laboratory research that has suggested alcohol can directly affect the kidneys," Schutte said.

Because the study is observational, it can only identify links between drinking habits and kidney injury, and cannot prove that beer or liquor directly caused the damage.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The authors also warned that the findings do not prove wine protects the kidneys, noting that drinking above 14 units per week, the U.K.’s recommended limit, was tied to higher risk across all drink types, including wine.

Additionally, participants relied on memory to report their average weekly alcohol intake, which can lead to inaccurate estimates or underreporting.

The study also only included adults ages 40 to 69, meaning the results may not apply to younger or older people.

articles.title: Data broker opt-out steps retirees need before the holidays
articles.summary:
Many retirees think they're protecting their privacy by staying off social media, removing their information from one people-search site or paying for credit monitoring. But a single data broker opt-out request may leave your home address, phone number and family details exposed elsewhere. With the holidays approaching, now is a good time to find out what's available about you online and take steps to remove it.

People-search sites like Spokeo, Whitepages and BeenVerified can make personal details available to strangers. Some information is free to view, while more detailed reports may require payment. And here's where it gets concerning. A scammer who knows your grandson's name or where your daughter lives could use those details to make a fake emergency call sound convincing. Here's where that information comes from, how to remove it and what you can do to help protect your family before the holidays.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES

You don't need a social media account to have your information collected. Data brokers gather information from public records, including property deeds, voter registration records where accessible and court filings. They may also obtain details from commercial databases, online activity and companies that collect personal information. Over time, those details can become part of a profile showing where you live, previous addresses, phone numbers and possible family connections.

According to the Federal Trade Commission, opting out of one people-search site doesn't remove your information from others. Your details may also reappear when public records change or websites collect updated information. For older adults, the financial risks can be especially serious. An FTC report released in October 2026 found that adults ages 60 and older reported approximately $3 billion in fraud losses during 2025. Although older adults reported losing money to fraud less frequently than younger adults overall, their reported individual losses tended to be higher.

You can use a free exposure scanner at CyberGuy.com to check whether your personal information appears on publicly searchable websites. Keep in mind that a free scan cannot uncover every private data broker database. The results might surprise you.

You can start removing your personal information yourself without paying for a service.

A credit freeze won't remove your information from data brokers, and credit monitoring generally alerts you to possible problems rather than preventing your details from appearing online. These tools serve different purposes.

One thing to remember: Removing your information from people-search sites doesn't erase public records. Your details may still appear in property records, court documents or even listings connected to family members. That's why it's important to check more than your own name. Doing this yourself can take hours, especially when you're dealing with multiple websites. And because data brokers continue collecting information, the work may need to be repeated.

DATA BROKER OPT-OUT: HOW RETIREES CAN PROTECT THEIR DATA

Before paying for a data removal service, there are two other options worth knowing about.

Google offers a free tool called Results about you that can help you find personal information appearing in Google Search. Depending on eligibility, you may be able to request the removal of results containing your home address, phone number or email address.

Here's how to get started:

Keep in mind that removing a Google search result doesn't delete the information from the original website. You may still need to contact the site directly.

If you live in California, you have another option. The state's free Delete Request and Opt-out Platform, called DROP, launched in January 2026. It allows eligible California residents to submit a single deletion request covering more than 600 registered data brokers.

Beginning Aug. 1, 2026, covered data brokers were required to start processing requests through the system. Removal can take time, and some information may be exempt under the law. You can submit a request and check its status at California's official DROP website at privacy.ca.gov/drop/. Other states also have privacy laws that may give residents additional rights to request deletion of their information.

WHY REMOVING YOUR DATA ONLINE MAY STILL LEAVE YOUR FAMILY EXPOSED

If you don't want to spend hours contacting websites and tracking removal requests, a personal data removal service can help.

These services contact data brokers on your behalf and submit requests to remove your personal information. Depending on the provider and plan, features may include:

Some services offer ongoing monitoring and follow-up requests, which can save time compared with handling each website yourself. It's important to understand that no service can guarantee every piece of personal information will disappear from the internet. Public records may remain accessible, and some websites may fall outside the service's coverage. Still, reducing the number of places where your information appears can make your personal details harder to find.

Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Thanksgiving brings families together, making it a great opportunity to talk about protecting everyone's personal information. You don't need to make it a lengthy discussion. A few simple checks can help everyone understand what scammers may already know about them.

After dinner, sit down with a family member and search your names on a few people-search sites. Look for home addresses, phone numbers and family connections. If you find something you don't want publicly available, discuss how to request its removal. Check your parents' information, too, with their permission. Even if you've removed your own details, your name or address may still appear in a relative's profile.

Choose a private phrase that family members can use if someone calls claiming there's an emergency. Avoid birthdays, pet names or other details someone could easily discover online. Agree on the phrase privately rather than sharing it in a group chat. A code word adds another layer of protection, but it shouldn't be your only way to verify someone's identity.

If someone claims to be a grandchild or another relative who urgently needs money, don't send anything until you've checked the story. Hang up and call your loved one directly using a phone number you already know. If you can't reach them, contact another trusted family member. Scammers can now use AI voice cloning to sound like someone you love. That means even a familiar voice may not be enough to prove who's calling. Learn more about how AI voice scams can clone your family's voice and what you can do to protect yourself. And be especially suspicious if someone demands payment through gift cards, cryptocurrency or wire transfers.

Agree that nobody will send emergency money based solely on an unexpected phone call or text. If something sounds suspicious, contact another family member before taking action. Scammers often pressure people to respond immediately or keep the situation secret. The more your family talks about these tactics ahead of time, the easier it becomes to recognize a suspicious request. Scammers may already know more about your family than you realize. A private code word adds protection, but always confirm an unexpected emergency by contacting your loved one directly before sending money.

Here's what concerns me. You can be careful about what you share online and still have your home address, phone number and family details available on people-search sites. Removing that information once is a good start, but it can show up again. That's why I recommend checking these sites regularly or using a trusted data removal service to help handle the work. And with Thanksgiving bringing families together, this is a great time to talk about scams and make sure everyone knows what to do if a suspicious call comes in. A few simple steps now could help keep your family's personal information out of the wrong hands.

Have you ever searched your name online and been surprised by how much personal information was available? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.
