articles.title: Duterte’s drug war is state-sanctioned, killed over 8,000 – Truth Commission
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – A week before former president Rodrigo Duterte’s historic trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) on November 30, a local truth commission released its initial report on his war on drugs.

The Philippine Truth and Reconciliation Commission (Truth Commission) said on Monday, November 23, that the so-called drug war was systemic and inflicted by Duterte’s government on thousands of victims.

“Preliminary, but enough to say plainly [that] the killings were state-organized. The official account cannot be accepted at face value. In the cases families brought to us, no one has been held to account,” said Truth Commission chairperson and former ICC judge Raul Pangalangan.

“When killings jump in the weeks after a president tells police he will protect them if they kill, when they fall almost to nothing each time the police are pulled out of the campaign, and when they continue through Christmas and All SoulsDay, the pattern points away from chance and toward policy,” the commission said in its report.

Duterte’s campaign promise in 2016 was to eliminate illegal drugs and criminality.

After he was sworn in as the 16th president in July, he immediately launched his drug war led by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and now fellow ICC co-accused, Senator Bato dela Rosa.

On his first day as president on July 1, 2016, Duterte told the PNP that even if they killed a thousand people in line of their duty, he will protect them.

Must Read

Duterte to PNP: ‘Do your duty and I will die for you’

Launched in May, the Truth Commission seeks to provide credible documentation of the killings linked to Duterte’s drug war. It held truth-telling sessions with the victims’ families to humanize drug war victims, analyze evidence, and demand accountability and reforms. Some of the findings came from these sessions, as well as from other sources.

On Monday, the commission said there were 8,230 people killed in the drug war, based on its initial count. This number is much higher compared to the government’s count.

“The governments most cited figure, 6,252, covers only deaths in police and PDEA (Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency) operations. The 12,000 to 30,000 range cited by the ICC Prosecutor draws on several published estimates. These figures count different things; no consensus exists on the number of the dead,” the commission explained.

Apart from the initial count, the commission also released the following key findings:

96.6% of the victims were men in their working and parenting years.

More than half or 56% of the killings were in Metro Manila and Central Luzon

Killings fell when police were pulled out from drug war operations.

24 of 46 exhumed victims had been shot in the head, while many killings bear the marks of execution.

People arrested during the drug war campaign remain in congested jails and prisons.

Play Video

The Truth Commission said its initial report will be available to everyone, including the Philippine government. Pangalangan said these findings will be shared to anyone who will find it useful, even national and international government and nongovernmental organizations.

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, who served as one of the reactors during the Truth Commission’s event, said they will look into the findings once transferred to the Department of Justice.

“These administrative investigations…. These are these are technically not final and definitive, right? As the pieces of evidence come along or made available, right? You adjust based on what’s…the truth and what’s available,” Vida said in a mix of Filipino and English.

Duterte has been detained in The Hague, the Netherlands, since March 2025 after he was arrested due to crimes against humanity. His case stemmed from his drug war and the killings allegedly committed by the Davao Death Squad.

On November 30, the former president will be the first Asian head of state to face a trial due to crimes against humanity before the ICC. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO – report
articles.summary:
WASHINGTON, USA – Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia’s recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China’s top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday, November 22.

Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

A spokesperson for Jensen Huang declined to comment. Spokespeople for Nvidia and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment.

Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns it smuggled Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China.

Sunday’s report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.

That October 29 article touched off a scandal that led to Jensen Huang’s resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia’s stock price.

Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.

“Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters,” Clayton told CNN’s “State of the Union” program. “And I’m going to let that investigation play out.”

The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington’s approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.

The affair between the two itself is of less interest, Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told NBC’s “Meet the Press.”

“I hope he had a good time,” Kennedy said on Sunday. “It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Marcoleta plunder case has not been dismissed
articles.summary:
Claim: The plunder case against Senator Rodante Marcoleta has been dismissed.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A reel posted on November 18 by the Facebook page Norbel Vidal shows Marcoleta standing at a lectern, with the text, “Demurrer to Evidence — tapos na ang kaso. Dismissed agad!” 

(Demurrer to Evidence — the case is over. Dismissed immediately!)

Additional text overlaid on the reel hints at Marcoleta’s supposed return to office now that the case against him has been junked.  

Several social media users welcomed the alleged development in the senator’s case, with some expressing their support for Marcoleta. As of writing, the post has garnered over 148,000 views, 4,200 reactions, 210 comments, and 369 shares.

The facts: There is no court ruling, official statement, or credible report showing that Marcoleta’s case has been dismissed. 

The reel was referring to a legal move by Marcoleta and his three co-accused — former lawmaker Michael Defensor and businessmen Aristotle Viray and Joseph Espiritu — who are seeking the dismissal of the P75-million plunder case against them.

On November 11, Sandiganbayan 3rd Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma confirmed that Marcoleta and his co-accused had filed motions for leave to file a demurrer to evidence. 

A demurrer to evidence asks a court to dismiss a case on the ground that the prosecution’s evidence is insufficient to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt. 

The misleading reel, however, frames Marcoleta’s legal move as though the court had already ruled to dismiss the plunder case.

Contrary to the claim, the senator’s case remains active. On November 23, the anti-graft court’s 3rd Division denied Marcoleta’s petition for bail, ruling that the evidence of guilt against him is strong — the threshold of evidence required for bail petitions. 

This ruling, however, is not a guilty verdict against Marcoleta and his co-accused. 

Marcoleta’s plunder case: The case against the lawmaker concerns P75 million in campaign donations Marcoleta received for his 2025 senatorial run, which the Ombudsman says he failed to declare in his Statement of Contributions and Expenditures and his Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth. (READ: How Marcoleta spent P112.9 million in his 2025 election campaign)

Marcoleta has rejected the allegations against him, arguing that they had no legal basis or merit.

The lawmaker has been suspended as a senator since October 19. He has been detained since July after surrendering to authorities following the issuance of a warrant for his arrest on plunder charges filed by the Office of the Ombudsman.

Aside from plunder, Marcoleta is also facing three counts of alleged violation of Presidential Decree No. 46 (receiving gifts).

False dismissal: Rappler has debunked other false claims about the senator: 

FACT CHECK: Supreme Court did not dismiss Marcoleta’s plunder case

FACT CHECK: Marcoleta and Estrada remain detained, contrary to claim

FACT CHECK: Marcoleta did not resign following ‘no’ vote in 2026 budget

FACT CHECK: Rodante Marcoleta is still senator

 – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024. 

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: COA questions Cebu government’s ‘heavy reliance’ on job order workers in 2025
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Audit (COA) has questioned the Cebu provincial government’s “heavy reliance” on job order (JO) workers in 2025.

COA said in its audit report that the Cebu provincial government had a total of 2,918 job order hires in 2025, or 68.24% of its total workforce of 4,276 that year.

It noted that in the same year, the Cebu government failed to fill up 1,789 vacancies in regular and casual positions.

The breakdown provided in the 2025 audit report showed the following:

Cebu Provincial Hospital (CPH)-Bogo City: 278 JOs vs 231 vacancies

Governor’s Office: 267 JOs vs 111 vacancies (including 67 permanent posts).

CPH-Danao City: 265  JOs vs 230 vacancies

CPH-Balamban: 257 JOs vs 228 vacancies

CPH-Carcar: 232 JOs vs 195 vacancies

“This heavy reliance on JO workers, despite the substantial number of unfilled regular and casual positions, indicates possible non-compliance with civil service rules and undermines the efficient utilization of government human resources,” the COA said.

The state auditor reminded the Cebu provincial government of the Local Government Code provision requiring local government units  to establish organizational structures and staffing patterns based on service requirements and financial capability, subject to applicable standards prescribed by the Civil Service Commission.

The COA and the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) earlier issued Joint Circular No. 2,. s of 2020 encouraging the priority hiring of qualified JO and contract of service personnel for unfilled plantilla positions.

Based on the COA’s count, 633 nurses were hired on JO basis even if there were 371 vacant posts.

JO workers also took professional and technical positions — nursing attendants, medical specialists, medical officers, midwives, and radiologic technologists — even when there were existing vacancies for these.

“The data indicate that a substantial number of professional and technical positions essential to hospital operations are being performed by JO workers while corresponding plantilla positions remain vacant. This arrangement reflects a mismatch between the approved staffing pattern and the actual workforce composition,” state auditors said.

While LGUs are authorized to tap JO workers when justified by operational requirements and available appropriations, such engagements should only complement the existing permanent workforce, rather than serving as substitute for the number of regular employees necessary to the delivery of government services.

Auditors also noted that while JO hires do not enjoy security of employment and do not enjoy standard benefits and entitlements of employees holding plantilla positions, they are nonetheless assigned to functions involving “professional, technical, and continuing services that are more closely aligned with plantilla or COS engagements.”

COA recommended that Cebu government undertake a comprehensive review of its staffing pattern to check the necessity of getting so many JO hires, and to prioritize the hiring of qualified JO workers for vacant positions.

In their response to the audit team, Cebu provincial officials informed COA that 42% of vacant permanent positions had been published, while 47 posts had been filled — 23 from JO hires. 

The Provincial Human Resource and Management Officer also reported that there were 1,013 vacant permanent positions under review as end-2025, and that 66 already filled. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Lacson flags ‘double’ appropriations for flood projects in 2027 budget
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson has flagged alleged double and triple appropriations for some flood control projects in the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, saying some of them had already received funding in previous years.

“Not only double, but some flood control projects even received triple budget allocations. They were funded in 2024, 2025, and 2026 but were still under the proposed budget in 2027,” Lacson told reporters on Monday, November 23.

These projects are separate from at least 30 alleged ghost multi-purpose buildings (MPBs) that the senator said he had identified in the proposed Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) budget under the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB).

Over the weekend, Lacson questioned the appropriations for 3,950 MPBs, apart from the 1,584 MPBs covered by the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) subprogram on financial assistance to local government units (LGUs) from 2022 to 2026.

Lacson said some of the MPBs appeared to be “ghost” projects. One infrastructure project, for instance, had received appropriations from 2024 to 2026, but no structure had been built at its designated site as of this year.

“Yes, we would move for its removal. That’s the logical thing to do,” Lacson said. “Why should we approve projects with massive allocations if they are not being established? Where are our public funds going?”

An initial investigation by Lacson’s office also found that the MPB projects involved alleged commissions of up to 10%. This is lower than the 15% to 30% kickbacks previously flagged in connection with anomalous flood control projects.

Must Read

House pushes thousands more multi-purpose buildings. Are they really needed?

Lacson said he would seek the removal of questionable infrastructure projects during the period of amendments to the budget bill.

“We continue to scrutinize the bill and find more of these kinds of appropriations. If there are double appropriations, one should be removed. If there are quadruple appropriations, three should be removed,” he added.

‘Papogi’ spending?

Lacson also criticized what he called “papogi spending” — spending meant to make one look good in the eyes of the public — in the proposed budget, including MPBs and P241 billion in what he described as “fragmented ayudas.”

Lacson questioned the continued funding of several government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP), Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD), and Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS).

However, he said he would not “necessarily” seek the removal of these programs.

“They were fragmented ayuda programs. We already have 4Ps, UniFAST, and tertiary education law,” Lacson said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Fuel prices going down for third straight week on November 24
articles.summary:
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going down for a third consecutive week starting Tuesday, November 24, as international oil prices continue to decline amid expectations of improving global supplies.

The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following minimum price decreases for November 24 to 30:

Gasoline – rollback of at least P3 per liter

Diesel – rollback of at least P2.60 per liter

Kerosene – rollback of at least P1.60 per liter

The adjustments follow last week’s reductions of P1.50 per liter for gasoline, P3.80 for diesel, and P5.80 for kerosene. Prior to that, gasoline prices plunged by P16.80 per liter, alongside rollbacks of P4.10 for diesel and P3.70 for kerosene.

This comes as global oil markets anticipate a supply surplus, with oil exports from the Middle East recovering and businesses and consumers cutting back on consumption.

However, the continuing US war on Iran and attacks on commercial vessels around the Strait of Hormuz remain risks to global supply.

Despite the recent rollbacks, local pump prices remain substantially higher than before the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at around P54 to P56 for gasoline, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene.

The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates.

Excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene have been suspended since late September, under Executive Order No. 125 issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Nearly 3,000 people petition gov't to prevent cheating on college entrance exam
articles.summary: Nearly 3,000 people have signed a petition demanding the government take proper steps to prevent cheating on the national college entrance exam, a student-led advocacy group said Monday, amid controversy over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating. The group, composed mainly of high school and college students, said it conducted two rounds of signature campaigns starting last Monday and a total of 2,964 people had joined the petition. Most of the signatories were students who had sat for the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday amid confusion over the government's announcement of haphazard measures to prevent AI-assisted cheating. The measures had been rolled out after the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam admitted to cheating using a miniature camera, a smartphone and generative AI. In the petition, the group said it demands the education ministry and relevant authorities clearly outline procedures for filing appeals and the criteria for invalidating scores in cases of cheating, among other measures.

articles.title: 2-term lawmaker nominated to lead interior ministry
articles.summary: Rep. Han Jun-ho, tapped to lead the interior ministry, is a two-term lawmaker of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) who formerly worked as a news anchor. Born in 1974 in the southwestern city of Jeonju, Han graduated from Yonsei University with a degree in mathematics before joining local broadcaster MBC as a newscaster in 2003. He left MBC in 2018 and worked at the presidential office under then President Moon Jae-in as a communications official. Han was elected as a lawmaker for the DPK in the 2020 general elections before winning his second term in the 2024 elections. He currently serves as a ranking member of the parliamentary science, ICT, broadcasting and communications committee. "As a two-term lawmaker and a former journalist, (Han) racked up legislative experience in various sectors, such as land, transport and artificial intelligence (AI)," Lim Kwang-hyun, presidential chief of staff, said. "He is expected to robustly secure public safety and inject vitality into region-led growth."

articles.title: 3-term lawmaker with N. Korea expertise tapped as unification minister
articles.summary: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo is a three-term lawmaker and a close political ally of President Lee Jae Myung with North Korea expertise. Born in 1967, he studied political science at Hanyang University. Before entering politics, he worked as a researcher at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and as a policy adviser to the Ministry of Unification. He also taught as a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. He won election to the National Assembly three times, serving from 2012 to 2024. Hong served as floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea from September 2023 to May 2024 when Lee was party chair. Earlier this year, Hong was appointed as senior presidential secretary for political affairs, handling coordination with the National Assembly and the political parties. At that time, the president described Hong as "reasonable and amicable," a lawmaker who "continuously practiced politics of tolerance and cooperation" in the belief that confrontation can be solved through "compromise and agreement." articles.title: Critic-turned-presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister
articles.summary: Kang Yu-jung, the senior presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister Monday, is a cultural specialist who worked for nearly two decades as a film and literary critic and columnist. Kang, 51, first gained prominence in 2005 when she swept three prizes in that year's newspaper literary contests, winning in film criticism from the Dong-A Ilbo and in literary criticism from the Chosun Ilbo and the Kyunghyang Shinmun. As a critic and columnist, Kang regularly appeared on television programs about film and wrote for daily newspapers. She also published several books on cinema and taught at Korea University and Kangnam University. Her interest in the arts extended beyond criticism. Last year, she received a special award at the Korea Dance Awards in recognition of her support for dance and her contributions to developing and popularizing the art form. Kang entered politics in the 2024 general election, winning a proportional representation seat with the Democratic Alliance of Korea, a coalition party led by the Democratic Party of Korea. articles.title: Ex-diplomat well versed in US, N. Korea tapped as foreign minister
articles.summary: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon, currently a senior presidential security official, is a former veteran diplomat well versed in relations with the United States and diplomacy with North Korea. Since President Lee Jae Myung took office in June last year, Lim has served as the second deputy director of the National Security Office at Cheong Wa Dae, assisting the president in making key foreign policy and security decisions. His nomination came as South Korea's chief diplomat faces a host of foreign policy tasks, ranging from implementing security, trade and investment agreements with the U.S. to handling North Korea-related diplomacy and ensuring cooperation with China, Japan and other countries. Since entering foreign service in 1988, Lim has served in various posts at home and abroad, including as ambassador to Canada, deputy consul general in New York, minister for political affairs at the embassy in Washington, and other posts in Austria, Italy, France and Spain. articles.title: Korea's exports forecast to exceed $1 tril. for 2nd straight year in 2027
articles.summary: Korea's exports are expected to exceed $1 trillion for the second consecutive year in 2027 on continued global demand for semiconductors, a state-run think tank said Monday. The Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade (KIET) forecast that Korea will post $1.32 trillion in exports in 2027, up 14.1 percent from this year's estimate of $1.16 trillion. The trade surplus is expected to rise to $455.9 billion next year from $377.8 billion this year. The KIET said exports are expected to expand 33.9 percent on-year in the first half of 2027, driven by increasing investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, while they are forecast to contract 0.7 percent in the second half due to a base effect and a correction in memory chip prices. As strong semiconductor exports are expected to boost domestic demand, the KIET projected Asia's fourth-largest economy will grow 3.5 percent next year. articles.title: S. Korea commemorates 16th anniv. of victory against N. Korea's 2010 shelling of border island
articles.summary: The Marine Corps on Monday held a ceremony to mark the 16th anniversary of South Korea's victory in an artillery attack in 2010 by North Korea on a border island that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The ceremony was held at Daejeon National Cemetery in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul, on the occasion of the 16th anniversary of the North's artillery attack on Yeonpyeong Island on Nov. 23, 2010. North Korea's shelling of the island marked its first attack on a civilian area in the South since the 1950-53 Korean War. During Monday's event, Vice Defense Minister Lee Doo-hee said the South Korean military will maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure its victory against any enemy threats. "Our military will immediately respond to any enemy threat or provocation and maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure absolute victory," Lee said in his commemorative address. "To achieve this, we will push to restructure the military system so that the Marine Corps will be enhanced to a quasi-fourth service," he added. articles.title: Court holds arrest warrant hearings for 8 election officials
articles.summary: A court on Monday held arrest warrant hearings for eight National Election Commission (NEC) officials accused of manipulating voter turnout numbers or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. Three officials from the NEC headquarters appeared at the Seoul Central District Court in the morning, refusing to answer reporters' questions before entering the courtroom. Hearings for the remaining five officials from regional NEC offices were set to be held later in the afternoon. The court was expected to decide whether to issue the warrants later in the day at the earliest. Requests for the warrants were filed Wednesday by special counsel Lee Tae-han's team on suspicions that the election officials entered false voter turnout figures while voting was under way or forged vote count sheets during the race for the education superintendent of Gyeonggi Province, with some of them allegedly involved in multiple cases. articles.title: Factional feud, impeachment fight test Kim Min-seok's DPK leadership at 100 days
articles.summary: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok heads into his 100th day in office on Tuesday, as party support slips amid a deepening factional feud, in stark contrast to the turnaround he promised. Kim pledged during his leadership campaign to raise the DPK’s support by at least 10 percentage points within three months. But a Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put the DPK’s support at 36 percent, down from 41 percent in a survey conducted from Aug. 11–13, just before Kim took office on Aug. 17. Under the circumstances, Kim’s leadership will face another test as he tries to reunite the DPK and win over centrist voters while the party’s hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae — a move that could rally its base and alienate moderates. “It appears the voters still don’t feel they can count on the ruling party to settle problems under Kim’s leadership,” said Jung Jae-hwan, a political science professor at Inha University. “The move to impeach the chief justice will test whether Kim can keep the party focused on voters’ everyd

articles.title: 5 CSAT examinees face criminal complaints over smart device cheating
articles.summary: The education ministry was set to file criminal complaints Monday against five people caught cheating with smart devices during last week's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), a senior ministry official said. The ministry previously announced that 111 suspected cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during the annual college entrance exam held Thursday amid growing public concerns over the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on national exams. Of those cases, five involved the actual use of devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras, according to the ministry. Complaints have already been filed against some of the five test-takers, and the process for all five will be completed before the day's end, Shin Jin-yong, head of the ministry's University Admissions Policy Division, said in a media briefing. The ministry also plans to indefinitely keep open its CSAT cheating reporting center on its website, Shin said, adding there are no restrictions on the scope of reports and that individuals can report suspected cheating not only in this year's CSAT

articles.title: Family of late LEET top scorer appears before police in cheating probe
articles.summary: A family member of the late top scorer of this year's law school entrance exam appeared before police Monday as investigators step up a probe into allegations that he cheated on the test. The late Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student, was found dead Thursday after facing suspicions of cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Despite his death, police have pressed ahead with the investigation on suspicion of fraud and other charges, after a group of lawyers earlier filed a police complaint. Earlier in the day, a family member of Lee appeared before the financial crime unit under the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. Police were expected to ask Lee's family member for cooperation in turning over evidence, such as his mobile phone. Lee's academic achievements came under widespread scrutiny following the recent admission by the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI. articles.title: Ex-Justice Minister Kang tapped as spy agency chief
articles.summary: President Lee Jae Myung nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service (NIS), Monday. Lee also tapped Lim Woong-soon, his second deputy national security adviser and a former ambassador to Canada, as foreign minister, and Hong Ihk-pyo, a former presidential secretary for political affairs and former floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), as unification minister. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the Cabinet reshuffle largely focused on the security and diplomacy sectors during a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul. He said the changes would bring in new leadership to protect Korea’s interests as the international landscape shifts. “Kang is the most suitable person to reinforce democratic oversight of the NIS, based on her strong belief in the neutrality of powerful organizations. She is also expected to resolve new security threats, such as cyberattacks, through international cooperation,” the chief of staff said. articles.title: Jongno District deploys AI crosswalks to give slower pedestrians more time
articles.summary: Jongno District in central Seoul is upgrading its intersections with artificial intelligence (AI), pavement-level LED lights and automated voice alerts to help pedestrians — especially children and older adults — cross streets more safely. The district office said it will begin operating pavement-mounted pedestrian signals and voice guidance devices at 123 locations from Dec. 1 with an AI-powered system that automatically extends crossing time. The pavement-level pedestrian signals illuminate the tactile pavers, a kind of ground surface indicator to assist disabled pedestrians, at crosswalks to help people detect when it is safe to cross. Voice guidance devices use infrared sensors to detect pedestrians and issue audible warnings when they attempt to cross against the signal, as well as announcing when the light turns green. The installations target roads with at least four lanes, prioritizing areas with heavy pedestrian traffic and a history of accidents. articles.title: US Forces Korea deploys Apache, Blackhawk helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan
articles.summary: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) recently deployed its helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan, the first time such assets have been sent outside the Korean Peninsula for exercises, the USFK said Monday. The 2nd Infantry Division's 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade deployed the AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, the UH-60 Black Hawk multirole utility helicopters and the CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters to the Combined Arms Training Center (CATC) at Camp Fuji, located in Shizuoka Prefecture, the USFK said in a social media post. It said the "historic first" deployment of the choppers was aimed at strengthening its readiness in the Indo-Pacific. The AH-64 Apache serves as a heavily armed attack helicopter designed to hunt and destroy enemy tanks and armored vehicles with missiles and rockets, while the UH-60 Black Hawk is a core asset primarily tasked with airlifting troops into combat zones, transporting supplies and evacuating wounded soldiers. The CH-47 Chinook is a heavy-lift transport helicopter used to move large numbers of troops, heavy artillery and bulk supplies across the battlefield.

articles.title: PPP files petition with Constitutional Court over special counsel bill
articles.summary: Lawmakers of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) filed a petition with the Constitutional Court on Monday, arguing that their rights to vote on legislation were violated by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)'s unilateral passage of a special counsel bill. The PPP's move came after the DPK-controlled National Assembly railroaded the bill earlier this month that mandates a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. PPP lawmakers had boycotted the vote in protest. The PPP claimed that its lawmakers were not given sufficient time to review and deliberate on the details of the bill before its passage and said it filed a competence dispute against National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and DPK Rep. Seo Young-kyo, chair of the parliamentary legislation and judiciary committee. articles.title: Seoul launches green bio hub to connect startups with investors, global markets
articles.summary: Seoul is expanding its ambitions in biotechnology, transforming its food startup center into a platform designed to connect promising agricultural and food technology companies with major corporations, investors and global distribution networks. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it had relaunched the Seoul Food Startup Center as the Seoul Green Bio Hub, broadening its focus from food manufacturing and distribution to technology-driven businesses built around agricultural and biological resources. Green biotechnology applies biological technologies to agricultural and other biological resources to create new products and commercial opportunities in sectors including food and agriculture. Of the 884 green bio companies registered nationwide with the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, 89 are based in Seoul, according to the city. The new hub will expand partnerships between startups and major corporations through open innovation programs, matching companies' technologies and ideas with corporate business needs and distribution networks. articles.title: Industry minister urges petrochem sector to rev up restructuring
articles.summary: The industry minister said Monday the petrochemical sector should accelerate its restructuring efforts to enhance its competitiveness. In August last year, 16 petrochemicals companies drew up business reorganization plans. Two restructuring schemes were approved by the government earlier this year, but a business reorganization plan for the Ulsan industrial complex has not been finalized. In a meeting with heads of major petrochemicals companies, such as LG Chem Ltd. and GS-Caltex Corp., Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan urged petrochemicals companies to draw up their final restructuring plans. "All companies should share the responsibility for the future of the sector," Kim said, adding that all discussions should be done before the end of the year. Kim said all necessary measures will be provided to help the sector take a leap forward to remain competitive. The local petrochemical sector has been facing a prolonged oversupply leading to low prices, especially amid the economic slowdown. articles.title: Chinese man gets suspended sentence for stealing 100 BTS concert wristbands to resell
articles.summary: A Chinese man in his 40s has received a suspended prison sentence for stealing 100 admission wristbands at a BTS concert venue in Busan with the intention of reselling them at inflated prices. According to legal sources Sunday, the Busan District Court sentenced the man, identified only as A, to 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, on charges of aggravated theft. The man was charged with stealing 100 admission wristbands from an event booth set up at the Busan Asiad Auxiliary Stadium in Yeonje District, Busan, at around noon on June 12, along with two unidentified accomplices. According to the court ruling, A arrived at Incheon International Airport the day before the theft and met with two accomplices to plan the resale of BTS concert tickets at inflated prices. However, the concert organizer had introduced measures to prevent ticket scalping, requiring attendees to present identification matching their mobile tickets before receiving admission wristbands. articles.title: 15 years, 164 awards: How Global Korea Award tracked changing Korea
articles.summary: In 2012, The Korea Times established the Korea Multicultural Youth Awards to encourage students from multicultural families who struggle with cultural differences and language barriers. Rebranded as the Global Korea Awards last year, the program marks its 15th anniversary this year. Over that span, it has recognized 152 students and individuals and 12 volunteer groups, teachers and institutions, distributing 164 awards in total. The Ministry of Gender Equality and Family has sponsored the program since its founding, and the grand prize winner receives the minister’s award. Among the honors is the Semoon Chang Award for students with outstanding foreign language skills, created in 2015 with column fees donated by Chang Se-moon, a former Korea Times columnist and retired economics professor at the University of South Alabama. Global Korea Award winners have played a key part in Korea’s multicultural youth community and continue to make their mark across a wide range of fields. articles.title: Sungkyunkwan University team develops ultrasensitive vitamin C sensor using AI
articles.summary: A Sungkyunkwan University research team has developed an ultrasensitive sensor capable of detecting even trace amounts of vitamin C by using artificial intelligence (AI) to optimize sensor fabrication conditions. The team was led by Park Jin-sung, a professor in the Department of Bio-Mechatronics Engineering, according to the university. A state-designated cultural heritage site, the building was converted into a public library in 2012. A public design competition will open Tuesday for the renovation of the library's four floors and an overhaul of its third-basement-floor archive, with the five floors spanning 7,556 square meters. To create a more spacious and open atmosphere, the city plans to relocate part of the library's current book collection from the upper floors to an underground storage area and install lower, more flexible bookshelves. NPA Commissioner General Kim Jong-chul made the pledge at his inauguration after Korea last month stripped prosecutors of their investigative powers, expanding the police role in criminal investigations. The study, published in the international journal iMeta, was led by Jwa Nam-soo, a professor in the university’s Department of Integrative Bioscience and Biotechnology. Researcher Nam Khoa Nguyen was listed as a co-first author, while Jwa was a co-corresponding author. The paper, titled “Decoding ferroptosis via integrated multi-omics analyses in rice blast,” examines ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death caused by iron-dependent oxidation of lipids, or fats, in cell membranes. Using integrated multi-omics analyses, the researchers identified contrasting roles of ferroptosis in plant immune responses and in the rice blast fungus’s infection process. articles.title: Pakistan has Portugal's 'full support' for GSP+ status, visiting FM says during delegation-level talks in Islamabad
articles.summary:
Pakistan has Portugal’s “full support” for the European Union’s (EU) GSP+ status, Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel said on Monday during Pakistan-Portugal delegation-level talks held in Islamabad.

Pakistan’s current GSP+ status is set to expire in 2027, after which Islamabad will seek a renewal.

GSP+ status is a special incentive awarded to developing countries to “pursue sustainable development and good governance” in exchange for cutting import duties to zero on two-thirds of the tariff lines of its exports.

The status was granted to Pakistan in 2014, resulting in a 108 per cent increase in Pakistani textile exports to the EU due to concessional tariffs.

In October 2023, the European Parliament unanimously voted to extend the GSP+ status for another four years until 2027 for developing countries, including Pakistan.

The upcoming GSP+ monitoring mission will scrutinise Pakistan’s record on 32 international conventions tied to the trade scheme. Maintaining GSP+ status is critical for Pakistan to keep export costs low.

Rangel, in his remarks, stressed that both Pakistan and the EU would mutually benefit from cooperation, adding that “we should not hesitate on developing these bilateral platforms”.

The Pakistani delegation was led by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

In his remarks, DPM Dar said, “Our focus is on strengthening our political ties, expanding bilateral trade and promoting investment.”

He proposed that the two countries regularly convene the Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum to help Pakistani and Portuguese companies “identify trading partners and explore joint venture opportunities”.

He also suggested that the two delegations identify proposals for progress and review implementation through bilateral political consultations.

The two ministers also agreed to set up a Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) between Pakistan and Portugal. Dar said the JMC would help promote business, trade and investment between the two countries by identifying the “hurdles” for consideration.

Dar added that he and his Portuguese counterpart agreed that parliamentary exchanges between the two countries should be considered as well.

Rangel said this was the first visit to Pakistan by a Portuguese delegation in 19 years.

“We look forward to enhancing our bilateral relationship in the economic area,” he said. He elaborated that a JMC would help “boost the economic dynamics of our relationship”.

Rangel praised Pakistan for its role as a “peace-building actor at a global level” as well as its efforts in Middle East diplomacy and the Palestine issue.

The visiting dignitary said that Portugal had a lot to learn from Pakistan, as it enters the United Nations Security Council.

The Portuguese FM added, “We really want to keep this bilateral political dialogue very intense during the two years that we will be holding a mandate in the Security Council of the United Nations because we know how attached Pakistan is to multilateralism, to the Charter of the United Nations, and to building peace and prosperity across the world”.

Referring to Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran conflict, Rangel said: “Without your mediation, we are fully aware that things would have been much more difficult than they are.”

He also acknowledged the Pakistani diaspora in Portugal, describing it as “a quite dynamic and well-integrated community”.

Concluding his remarks, the Portuguese FM described his visit to Pakistan as “very fruitful and very positive”.

Rangel-Dar meeting

Previously, Rangel reaffirmed his country’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations with Pakistan, a statement by the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Rangel made these remarks during a meeting with DPM Dar at the FO in Islamabad, where the Portuguese minister arrived on Sunday on a two-day visit.

In today’s meeting, Rangel and Dar reviewed the “longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Portugal as the two countries mark 77 years of diplomatic relations”, the FO statement said.

It added that DPM Dar stressed the importance of enhanced diplomatic engagement, parliamentary exchanges and regular consultations through existing bilateral mechanisms.

For his part, Rangel reaffirmed Portugal’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties, thanked Pakistan for its support at the United Nations and appreciated the contribution of the Pakistani diaspora in Portugal to promoting closer ties between the two countries, the statement said.

“Both leaders also exchanged views on regional developments and discussed cooperation at the UN and within the European Union framework,” it said.

Moreover, Rangel appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability”, the statement said, adding that the two leaders also emphasised the importance of dialogue, diplomacy and effective multilateralism in addressing shared challenges.

During his time in Pakistan, Rangel is also scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with DPM Dar. He is accompanied by a business delegation for the inaugural Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum.

The FO earlier said the visit would also feature a Pakistan-Portugal Business Forum, and companies from both countries would hold business-to-business meetings to explore commercial partnerships and investment opportunities in agri-food, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals, information technology and textiles.

Following his arrival on Sunday, Rangel praised Pakistan’s peace efforts in recent months during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

“The world needs you. We have been seeing in the very recent months that the role of Pakistan is decisive for global peace, so we count on you to help all the peoples of the world, reaching peace and prosperity,” he said while speaking to state-run Pakistan TV.

Visa exemption for diplomatic passport holders

According to a separate FO statement, DPM Dar and Rangel signed an agreement on the mutual exemption of visa requirements for holders of diplomatic passports between the two countries.

“The agreement will facilitate high-level engagement, diplomatic exchanges and further strengthen the longstanding and friendly relations between Pakistan and Portugal,” FO said.

articles.title: 7 killed, 2 injured as stone-laden truck overturns onto mini-truck in Bahawalpur
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Seven people were killed and two others were injured when a stone-laden truck hit a mini-truck and overturned onto it in Bahawalpur’s Uch Sharif early on Monday morning, an official and Rescue 1122 said.

Bahawalpur District Police Officer (DPO) Rana Abdul Wahab told Dawn that the mini-truck, travelling from Dera Ghazi Khan to Khairpur Tamewali, was carrying 16 people and stopped along a highway due to fog.

“The driver was cleaning the windscreen of the stationary vehicle when another truck, laden with stones, hit it and turned over onto it,” the DPO said.

According to the official, the driver of the stone-laden truck, which was also travelling from Dera Ghazi Khan, had lost control of the vehicle.

Passengers in the mini-truck were left trapped, he said.

A Rescue 1122 statement said the passengers were trapped under the truck and the stones, and an excavator was used to clear the stones.

The DPO said police and rescue personnel were able to rescue nine people while seven died because of injuries.

According to Rescue 1122, two people have been injured among those rescued.

DPO Wahab said the driver of the stone-laden truck had fled the scene after the accident. “However, police have identified him and registered a case at Dhoorkot police station. Raids are being conducted to arrest the suspect,” the DPO said.

Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the loss of lives in the accident, Associated Press of Pakistan reported.

In a message, the CM extended her “heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families,” praying for their strength and patience to bear the “irreparable” loss.

CM Maryam also sought a detailed report on the accident and directed relevant authorities to provide the necessary details, according to APP.

Earlier this month, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan.

On Oct 21, ten people were killed and 44 others injured when a passenger bus overturned after hitting a road divider on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur district’s Rojhan tehsil.

On Oct 19, a road accident on Multan’s Bosan Road claimed the lives of five men in their 20s after their speeding Toyota Corolla hit a road divider before crashing into the wall of a nearby plot and catching fire.

articles.title: Asif says process for referendum on new provinces likely to move forward early next year
articles.summary:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said discussions on a possible referendum to create new provinces are expected to take a “definitive shape” by the end of this year, with the process likely to move forward early next year.

Speaking on ARY News programme ‘Sawal Yeh Hai’ on Sunday, Asif said the matter would not take long to reach a conclusion, though he refrained from giving a specific date.

Asked whether the PML-N and the federal government had reached a principled decision on holding a referendum, and what its timeline and outline would be, he said: “Perhaps by the year-end, all this debate and discussion that is taking place will take some definitive shape. What shape it will take, I cannot say, but it won’t take long. I can certainly say that it is not going to take two to four months.”

He said the date could be a few days earlier or later, but the process was expected to move forward soon.

“God willing, but it would not be appropriate for me to give a date. I cannot provide a definitive timeline, but, based on my understanding, the inevitability of this is becoming clearer day by day,” he said.

Asked how the referendum question would be framed, given opposition from one province and the fact that previous referendums had been held under dictatorships, Asif said everyone had the right to express reservations.

“You cannot deny someone that right if they have reservations about the entire matter and are expressing them. That is a fundamental part of a democratic society,” he said.

He said a joint document would be prepared with input from all stakeholders to ensure that the proposal was acceptable to everyone.

“It will be a joint document in which all the stakeholders will have their input. Rather than producing a document that falls prey to disagreement, my own view is that the efforts and back-and-forth meetings currently taking place will produce something that is acceptable to all,” he added.

Asked whether the government would seek consensus on the referendum question to bring the PPP on board, Asif said that was precisely the intention.

He said the question would outline the purpose and objectives of the proposed exercise, requiring people to respond with a yes or no. These objectives, he added, would also be defined through consensus.

Regarding the constitutional requirements for holding a referendum, he said the Constitution provided for such an exercise but also laid down the procedure for constitutional amendments, which could not be bypassed.

“There is room for a referendum in the Constitution; there is no doubt about that. However, the procedure for a constitutional amendment is also laid down in it, and no one can deviate from that procedure,” he said.

The defence minister said the proposed changes could have far-reaching positive consequences, noting that Pakistan had previously altered its administrative map through the creation of One Unit and the subsequent establishment of provinces.

He expressed confidence that the joint preparation of a document would address reservations and prevent major disagreements.

“I think politics is the art of the possible, and this will definitely be made possible, God willing,” he added.

Asif had made similar remarks a few days earlier, saying he believed that a consensus was being developed on the creation of new provinces and that the process was moving towards culmination.

Speaking on Geo News, he had said the new year would bring a new system and that reaching consensus could lead to a progressive change in the country’s political landscape. He had also advocated a robust local government system, saying smaller administrative units would help improve public service delivery.

The remarks come amid a debate over the proposed creation of new provinces, with Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisting last week that a referendum on the matter “will happen”.

The issue gained renewed attention after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari opposed the creation of new provinces and the proposed referendum in a speech on Tuesday, warning that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces.

Over the past few months, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi has whipped up a political storm since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On November 12, Naqvi also floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

articles.title: India to give $1.62bn economic package to flood-hit Nepal
articles.summary:
India will give Nepal an economic package worth 240 billion Nepalese rupees ($1.62bn), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday, after talks with his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.

Shah is in the Indian capital for a two-day visit, his first bilateral trip since coming to power in March, and in the aftermath of the devastating Himalayan flood in August that killed some 1,500 people, with another 5,200 missing and presumed dead.

“Today, to give fresh impetus to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development, we are announcing a development cooperation package worth 24,000 crore (240 billion) Nepalese rupees,” Modi said, addressing the media after the talks, with Shah standing beside him.

“Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said.

Shah thanked India for consistently acting as a first responder for Nepal “in times of natural disasters and difficult hours”.

“I warmly welcome Indian investors to Nepal to partner in the economic prosperity of our two countries in the coming days,” he said, and invited Modi to visit the Himalayan nation.

The two countries signed agreements to boost their economic relationship and Modi and Shah jointly opened a train link connecting the two countries.

The August 26 flood, caused by a glacier collapse on Nepal’s border with China, sent a mass of mud and rock crashing into the Trishuli river.

The resulting flood washed away villages, snapped highways, bridges and power lines, and buried homes in the mud in the impoverished country that is wedged between Asian giants India and China.

Nepal and India enjoy longstanding cultural, economic and people-to-people ties with an open border allowing hundreds of thousands of Nepalis to live and work in India.

New Delhi was the first to respond after the August flood, sending several plane-loads of aid to restore communication links that were severed in the mountains.

articles.title: Shujaat, Naqvi discuss creation of new provinces, devolution of power in Lahore meeting
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers came under discussion on Monday when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain at his residence in Lahore.

The meeting comes amid an ongoing political debate over the creation of new provinces, with several political leaders pushing for a nationwide referendum to settle the matter.

It was sparked by Naqvi’s July remarks, wherein he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

In Monday’s meeting, the two leaders discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry after the meeting.

During the discussion, Shujaat said the question of creating new provinces was directly linked to public convenience, good governance, administrative efficiency and the country’s future.

“Strengthening existing administrative units and making them more empowered can also be an effective way to address governance-related challenges. The biggest stakeholders of Pakistan are its ordinary people,” Shujaat was quoted as saying, adding that decisions should be made in accordance with the aspirations of the people.

“If we do not take steps in the right direction today, tomorrow will not forgive us,” he remarked.

Naqvi said it was imperative to take all decisions in accordance with the wishes of the people of Pakistan. The interior minister also briefed the PML-Q leader on the government’s counterterrorism and peacekeeping measures in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain and Punjab Minister for Industries Chaudhry Shafay Hussain were also present at the meeting.

The meeting comes as Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisted last week that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen” amid the debate on new provinces.

In his remarks on Friday, Chaudhry had maintained that the PML-N would undertake “every last effort” to convince the PPP.

“A referendum is neither non-constitutional nor undemocratic; the public’s opinion can be sought on any important matter,” he had said.

Chaudhry’s remarks came after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari delivered a no-holds-barred speech earlier last week that covered the question of new provinces.

Bilawal had expressed his opposition to the creation of provinces and the idea of holding a referendum for such a move in his speech. He cautioned that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly in Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

However, the federal government maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional method of gauging public opinion on new provinces and that no political party should have reservations regarding it.

articles.title: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
articles.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.

The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines.

But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”.

“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky wrote on X.

The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war”.

“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added.

A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelensky said.

Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian.

The UN mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”.

“Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X.

UN calls for probe into attacks

The United Nations called for an independent investigation into the drone attacks, expressing concern over the potential spillover of the Ukraine war into Libya.

Authorities said all crew members had been rescued and were receiving treatment for minor injuries. They said a merchant vessel had been targeted by explosive-laden sea drones off Benghazi but did not identify its country of origin. Reports said the second ship was sailing under a Maltese flag.

Libya Alhadath television later reported that naval and air force units had intercepted more than 12 explosive-laden sea drones off Benghazi.

Libya’s eastern administration did not identify those responsible for the attack but said the country was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

Meanwhile, Ukraine said on Monday that Russian strikes had killed at least 12 people in its Kyiv region, including in a block of flats and at a supermarket.

The conflict, which began with Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

‘Shadow fleet’

Earlier reports said a fire broke out inside an ammunition depot at a naval base, but authorities in Libya’s east said later “the explosion occurred on board a Russian ship docked in the port”.“It is suspected that the ship was attacked by drones,” an official statement said.

“The ship was en route back to Russia and its stop was for refuelling and resupply.” The eastern administration said it would launch a joint investigation with Russia.

The rival UN-recognised government in Tripoli said in a statement it was alarmed by “risks posed by involving civilian ports and facilities in activities linked to external conflicts”.

In March, a Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast following an attack, which Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed on Ukraine. The vessel was part of Russia’s so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers that carry its oil and gas around the world, skirting Western restrictions.

Ukraine has at times admitted to attacking Moscow’s shadow fleet, including in the Mediterranean last December.

The Tripoli government said it rejected any attempt to turn Libya into “an arena for international conflicts” and the use of its territory “for any military or logistical activities that could jeopardise” national security or sovereignty.

Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

It remains divided between the government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar.

articles.title: ADB invests in Pakistan-based B2B fintech company Neem
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Monday said it invested an undisclosed amount in Neem, a Pakistan-based B2B fintech company that helps businesses receive, manage, and pay out money digitally.

In a statement, the Manila-based lending agency said its investment will flow through ADB Ventures, the venture capital arm of the ADB.

The seed investment will support Neem’s product development, help expand its team, and accelerate the onboarding of enterprise and merchant clients across Pakistan, the ADB said.

Pakistan has made strong progress in digitising consumer payments, with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP)’s instant payment system, Raast, and mobile wallets bringing millions of people onto digital rails. Business payments, however, have not kept pace.

According to SBP, an estimated 71 per cent of retail transaction value is still settled in cash, and companies looking to go digital must integrate separately with banks, wallets, payroll providers and reconciliation tools, a process that can be slow, costly, and hard to scale.

Neem aims to close this gap by giving businesses a single platform to manage how money comes in, how it is tracked, and how it is paid out. Its API-first system combines collections, disbursements, a programmable ledger and finance workflows, and connects directly with a company’s existing operating systems to automate settlement and reconciliation in real time.

Neem currently serves more than 70 enterprise clients across logistics, utilities, insurance, manufacturing and retail.

“Pakistan is laying a strong foundation for digital payments, and the next step is ensuring that businesses of all sizes can fully benefit from this progress,” said Emma Fan, ADB Country Director for Pakistan.

“Neem is helping enterprises move away from cash and fragmented systems toward payment solutions that are faster, more transparent and easier to manage.”

The impact extends well beyond the enterprises Neem serves directly. As businesses digitise their payments, the suppliers, small merchants and gig workers they pay are brought into the formal financial system.

Neem’s solutions are built to meet the payment needs of businesses of every size, including women-owned businesses and micro-entrepreneurs, so access to modern financial infrastructure is not limited to large enterprises.

As part of its lending portfolio, Neem also gives employees responsible access to wages they have already earned. The offering focuses on blue-collar workers in industries that employ large workforces across Pakistan and helps reduce reliance on informal borrowing.

ADB Ventures invests in early-stage technology companies building solutions that address the most pressing challenges across Asia and the Pacific, with a focus on sectors including financial technology, agricultural technology, climate resilience and inclusive growth.

articles.title: Trump hosts gala for meme coin investors as his token plunges to record lows
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump has made hundreds of millions from his $TRUMP meme coin, but at a Sunday dinner for the token’s biggest holders, he said his motive for supporting the cryptocurrency was to boost the economic competitiveness of the United States.

“I’m doing it for the United States… If we don’t do it, China’s going to do it,” Trump told attendees at his golf club outside Washington.

It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 but has fallen to a record low of under $1.

The private dinner this year was more low-key than the initial event last year, attendees said, with a smaller crowd and far less money at stake this time. Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP coin from Sept 30 to Nov 16.

Organisers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday’s dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on Nov 16.

Together, those listed wallets only held $8.6 million — a shadow of the $148 million listed for the dinner in May 2025, which was ​attended by 220 wealthy crypto investors.

Sunday’s participants stood in the rain as they waited to enter the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia. Attendees described the scene inside as subdued.

It was a far different atmosphere from the first gala, when tuxedo-clad contest winners pulled up to the club in luxury sports cars, and protesters chanted and stomped outside the club as the presidential Marine One helicopter descended.

The May 2025 event’s biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5m of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing autographs.

Attendees were able to dine on grilled filet mignon and pan-seared halibut while hearing speeches from the likes of Kevin O’Leary of Shark Tank television show and NBA veteran Tristan Thompson.

According to the contest’s website, the top 29 winners would join a VIP reception with the president and receive a gift bag with Trump swag. The top four also would get an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch.

Morten Christensen, founder of cryptocurrency platform Airdrop Alert, said he qualified for the top 29 with $41,000 of time-weighted $TRUMP holdings by using a hedging strategy — buying and selling the token using perpetual futures — that ensured he did not lose any money.

But he was denied a VIP band at the event, Christensen said.

“I asked like five people from the staff” and was told to email customer support, he said on Sunday night.

“Obviously, no one is going to reply right now,” said Christensen, who added that he was kicked out of the event around 7pm for “sharing with the press.”

He waited outside in the rain for his sister, who was still inside.

The Trump Meme Coin project and the White House did not respond to requests for comment.

Meme coin tumbles

More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis.

But the $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family itself at least $635 million, according to the presidents June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3 billion through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

The president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.

articles.title: Bad COP, worse COP: What’s next after climate talks fail?
articles.summary:
The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries.

The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies.

It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”.

For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus.

“Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme.

Bowen identified the same issue.

“The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said.

“That’s a very tough ask.”

‘Significant reform’

Sunday’s collapse has renewed calls for a reform to that consensus-based process, in which any one country, or a small minority, can nix progress.

“It has been clear for years that the COP process is in need of significant reform,” wrote former US vice-president Al Gore on X.

He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.”

But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms.

He described that as a “particular challenge”, although others might characterise it as simply impossible.

The COP31 talks deadlocked over multiple issues, notably whether the so-called cover decision would mention phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels.

Several countries refused a deal without that mention, while others including Saudi Arabia were vehemently opposed to its inclusion.

There were other serious fault lines, including the timing of scientific work from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and language on carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by some as costly and ineffective.

Crucially for developing countries, there was also no progress on finance — the money badly needed to help countries transition energy systems and adapt to the natural disasters climate change is already worsening.

“The fundamental problem for globally agreed climate policy is more starkly obvious than ever: fossil fuel powers will not agree to have their resource wealth devalued, and rich countries won’t provide enough climate finance to the developing world,” said Frank Jotzo, professor of environmental and climate change economics at the Australian National University.

‘Doesn’t replace COP’

Other COPs have ended in failure before, including most recently in 2009.

But for all the forum’s failings, most agree that the COP process remains important for its unique format, bringing together virtually every country in the world and offering equal billing to all.

As a result, few suggest the process should be abandoned, but there are growing calls for alternatives to advance climate change action, including legal suits.

That route is already being pursued, most notably with an International Court of Justice advisory opinion that confirmed states have a binding legal obligation to combat climate change.

“If the negotiations are not delivering what individual states need, then they’ll certainly consider turning to the ICJ and other international courts,” said Harj Narulla, an international lawyer who advised the Solomon Islands at COP31.

Others expect growing interest in agreements made outside the COP process, like the Santa Marta initiative, bringing together countries committed to phasing out fossil fuels.

The process grew out of the COP30 meeting in Brazil, where interested nations sought to bypass a lack of consensus on the issue.

Members held talks earlier this year, and agreed some first steps, including an expert scientific panel to advise on pathways.

These “plurilateral processes are growing,” said Jotzo, and more are needed, including on carbon removal technologies and finance for adaptation.

Bowen too said he sees the Santa Marta process becoming “increasingly important.”

“Doesn’t replace COP. It’s just another way of doing it,” he added.

articles.title: Any talks with India on terrorism must be 'evidence-based', says Musadik Malik
articles.summary:
Federal minister Musadik Malik said on Sunday that any dialogue between Pakistan and India on terrorism must be “based on evidence”.

Malik is in New Delhi on a three-day trip to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, making him the first Pakistani minister to visit the neighbour since former foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari attended an SCO meeting in May 2023.

Pakistan has repeatedly offered to hold talks with India to resolve outstanding disputes, including the water issue.

In video clips shared by India’s ANI news agency on Sunday, Malik responded to queries from Indian media and stressed that he had repeatedly presented Pakistan’s stance before the reporters.

“I am giving you a stable response that whenever discussions take place, they will be based on evidence, and they will certainly happen,” he affirmed, saying if New Delhi wanted a “lasting solution”.

“You must also have some issues, [though] our issues are much greater than yours, and we also need a lot of evidence […] Whenever dialogue takes place, it will be based on evidence,” the climate change minister reiterated.

Malik said Pakistan had repeatedly stated that evidence relating to terrorism could be presented through both bilateral and multilateral forums. “You may bring evidence; we also have evidence that we want to present,” he added.

India’s foreign minister had said in June 2024 that his country wanted to “find a solution to the issue of years-old cross-border terrorism” with Pakistan. However, a military conflict between the neighbours last year intensified tensions and escalatory rhetoric from India.

In May 2025, a four-day confrontation between Pakistan and India was sparked by an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam, which New Delhi, without evidence, linked to Pakistan.

Islamabad had strongly denied responsibility while calling for a neutral investigation.

In another clip, Malik noted that India had invited a representative from Pakistan to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, a multilateral event.

“I am your guest. You invited me to a specific forum; I am present before you. I answered all those questions you asked about this forum,” the minister said, remarking that he had conveyed the “voice of my heart” to the people across the region through the forum.

Malik stated, “You are today asking me questions for which you did not invite me. When you invite me for that question, I will appear. However, you first ought to invite me and say ‘we want to speak bilaterally with you’.”

‘Will speak on IWT when invited to do so’

The minister was also asked about his remarks on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), but said he would comment on the matter when invited to do so.

“You have currently invited me to speak on topics about which I have already spoken, that when temperatures rise, climate is destroyed, Glofs happen.
